query: Which country was the first to formally authorise the consumption of in vitro cultured meat, and in which month and year?
answer: The country that was the first to formally authorise the consumption of in vitro cultured meat is Singapore. According to the text, the first cultured chicken nuggets were approved for market entry in Singapore in December 2020.

Background 
Placing meat on the market made from in vitro cultured animal cells (cultured 
meat) is currently not formally authorised in Europe. Cultured meat is considered 
a novel food within the European Union (EU), whose market authorisation is only 
allowed after a safety assessment by the European Food Safety Authority (EFSA), 
followed by approval by the European Commission (EC) and the EU Member 
States.

Findings 
Legal framework  
The term ‘cultered meat’ refers to meat products grown in vitro from animal cells. 
Cultured meat is a novel food in the European Union and is currently not allowed 
to be placed on the market. The European Commission, together with the EU 
Member States, dec ides on the authorisation of novel foods to the European 
market, following a food safety risk assessment by EFSA. The European
